reviews.comment: Fast lectures that are hard to keep up with. Office hours with the professor are clear and helpful. Content is more or less alright and the exams are not very difficult.

Overall he's a great guy, highly suggest going to his office hours and working with him to schedule times to meet with him. He always tried his best to help me and make sure I understood the information before I left his office. While he does care about his students passing, his lecturer style is extremely fast and hard to keep up with.

Nice guy, awful lecturer. Talks and writes super fast, and reading the textbook chapter ahead of time is almost a requirement to understand them. He's nice outside of lectures, offering extra office hours and was super nice about rescheduling my final, but if you're not a big self-studier you should avoid him.

Great guy but he usually goes fast in lectures. He is very smart which might backfire sometimes as he skips steps and uses tricky techniques to solve equations. Very willing to help out students and will patiently clarify multiple times if needed. Tests were a little difficult but if you can do the homework they are pretty doable.

Differential Equations is a difficult class as it is, but Dr. Liu does his absolute best to help his students understand and master the material. He is a very generous grader on the exams, and he is available outside of his class to help his students as well. I would highly recommend taking Dr. Liu for MATH 308.
unreadable handwriting, heavy accent, very difficult exams, not similar to hw at all. AVOID AVOID AVOID!!

If you are not ready to self study Diff Eq, either thought the text book or videos, Do not take this prof. He uses obscure notation and expects you to know it day one and writes way too fast on the white board. The grading is pretty similar from prof to prof for 308 at TAMU so that is no different.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Horrid lectures, just scribbles on a board and explanations are very confusing. His lectures probably killed some of my brain cells. Provided notes on canvas are illegible. His notes uses Greek symbols as substitutes for two word and never explained what they meant until someone asked, and I'm pretty sure there's 50 more we still don't know.

'Actually took Differential equations'. Very present during lectures, never reading of slides, you can tell he knows what he is doing and that he likes doing it as well. He was always available for questions both in and outside the classroom. While the tests were difficult and do take up most of your grade he does provide great practice problems.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: This professor has an accent and sometimes has problems explaining things in English. If you have trouble understanding people with accents or something else along those lines, don't take this professor. Also, attendance may not be mandatory, but he if lecture attendance is low, he will ramp up the difficulty of questions on the final as punishment

He's a really nice guy and everything but he can be hard to understand at times and his lectures were anything but helpful. You're better off teaching yourself the material outside of class which I always did. The tests are another matter since the math department makes them, but he really does little to prepare you for them.
reviews.ratingTags: Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS
